item.summary: fix(gateway): frozen worker processes never resume when the host ps stalls (#123976) * fix(gateway): bound quiescence identity lookups so thaw cannot hang processIdentity() ran `ps` through execFileSync with no timeout, while its two siblings in the same script (processes(), processStatus()) both pass timeout: 2000. Every thaw path gates on it — resumeProcesses(), the watchdog expiry loop, and REMOTE_WORKSPACE_RESUME_JS all call processIdentity before each SIGCONT — so a host whose `ps` stalls leaves the entire lease frozen with no remaining resumer. SIGSTOP cannot be caught, so those processes never run again and never release their memory. Bring processIdentity to parity with its siblings. Measured with the exported scripts against a fixture whose `ps` stalls on the identity lookup: unbounded resume was still hung when a 20s cap killed it (exit 124); bounded resume fails in 2s with `spawnSync ps ETIMEDOUT`. * fix(gateway): thaw frozen processes before retiring the quiescence watchdog A bounded identity lookup still fails on a stalled host ps. Resume retired the watchdog first, so an aborted sweep left the lease with no resumer at all and the frozen workers stopped forever. Thawin
